title: 1964 Greater London Council election
summary: The first election to the new Greater London Council, which replaced the London County Council and extended London-wide government out to the suburbs. Labour, led by Bill Fiske, won a majority with 64 of the 100 seats. The new councillors took office when the GLC formally came into being in 1965.
highlights: First-ever election to the Greater London Council
Labour wins a majority with 64 of 100 seats
Bill Fiske becomes the first leader of the GLC
The GLC replaced the London County Council and covered all 32 new London boroughs

council.note: 100 councillors elected from borough-based multi-member electoral areas, plus 16 aldermen chosen by the council. The Greater London Council formally took over from the London County Council on 1 April 1965. Vote totals are all ballots cast under the multi-member bloc vote (each elector had one vote per seat); the percentage shares recorded by Rallings & Thrasher use a slightly different basis.
